Subject: Follow-up: RAG pilot fit discussion + recommended next steps

Hi Sana — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have shared alignment and proposed next steps.

Recap
- Primary objective: surfacing region-specific clinical guidance snippets inside clinician EMR workflows (~200ms median latency target for short answers).
- Data shape: 350k clinical notes, mostly discharge summaries and consult notes; expect average doc chunk length ~350 tokens.
- Quality guardrails: high precision for grounding (cite source + paragraph-level provenance); F1-type metrics are helpful but we emphasized precision at top-1 and hallucination rate <3%.

Initial model & retrieval recommendations (high-level)
- Embeddings: use redwood/embed-stable-english-32k (good tradeoff for clinical recall in our internal tests).
- Retriever: hybrid approach — vector store (FAISS IVF/PQ) for semantic recall + BM25 for short literal matches. Chunk size: 300 tokens with 50-token overlap.
- Reranker: cross-encoder pairwise reranker (redwood/ranker-cross-bert-large) for top-10 re-ranking — gives best P@1 in our pilot runs.
- Generator: recommend trying clarity-7b-qa-q4 (low-latency, quantized) for initial latency/cost curve; fallback to clarity-13b if output quality is insufficient.

Attachments I uploaded for your review: aurora_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts we discussed) and a short summary of preliminary benchmarks. Links below.

Proposed next steps
1) Camila to run a focused RAG micro-benchmark on a 5k sample (we propose the sample + prompt set attached) — target delivery by EOD Thu.
2) You to confirm two compliance items: (a) required retention window for logs, (b) whether PHI will be sent to hosted vs private deployment.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical pilot kickoff (Camila + infra) next week to validate vector store config and reranker latency.

Can you confirm the sample is representative and whether procurement needs a standard SOW before we run the micro-bench?

Thanks — Rishi

Subject: Technical note: retrieval config, reranker tradeoffs, and grounding metrics

Hi Sana — short technical note from our side after reviewing your constraints.

1) Retrieval config- Chunking: 300 tokens / 50 overlap — reduces split-sentence misses and keeps retrieval latency predictable.- Index: FAISS IVF-PQ for cost-effective nearest-neighbor; tune nlist to ~4096 for 350k docs.- Hybrid recall: combine BM25 score + cosine similarity with a small weight multiplier (0.2) to favor exact matches for short queries.

2) Reranker choice- Cross-encoder (pairwise) gives the best grounding precision but is heavier. We recommend redwood/ranker-cross-bert-large for the pilot.- Hybrid option: a clinical bi-encoder (redwood/embed-clinical-768) for candidate pruning to top-50, then cross-encoder for final top-10 — reduces cross-encoder calls by ~80% in our logs.

3) Grounding metrics (how we’ll measure quality)- Top-1 Precision (source-citation correct), Top-3 Precision, Hallucination rate (binary label per response), Answer latency (p50/p95).

4) Prompt set note- We reviewed your provided samples — some prompts include multi-part instructions that reduce grounding; we recommend explicit "Cite the paragraph and source" postfix in operational prompts (see aurora_prompt_set_v1.csv).

Action items from Camila
- I’ll run the 5k micro-benchmark with both pure cross-encoder and hybrid reranker flows; will attach raw P/R metrics and call-level latencies by Fri EOD.
- If the hosted retention window is ok for you, Rishi can share an upload link and we will ingest only the masked sample.

If any of the above looks off, flag it and I’ll adjust.
